title: Lignin Down-regulation of Zea mays via dsRNAi and Klason Lignin Analysis
protocol: Design gene-specific primers for dsRNAi constructs to knock out the ZmCCR1 gene, including necessary restriction enzyme sites.
Amplify a 523 bp fragment from nucleotide 748 to 1271 of ZmCCR1 cDNA by PCR using primers ZmCCR1_748F_BglII and ZmCCR1_1271R_NcoI.
Amplify a 285 bp fragment from nucleotide 986 to 1271 of ZmCCR1 cDNA by PCR using primers ZmCCR1_986F_BglII and ZmCCR1_1271R_SacI.
Ligate each amplified fragment individually into pGEM-T Easy following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Isolate mini-prep plasmid DNA from individual transformants containing the pGEM-T constructs using a commercial kit.
Digest both pGEM-T::ZmCCR1 (523 bp) and IV-1.1 (cytoplasm expression vector) with BglII and NcoI enzymes.
Ligate the large digested gel-purified ZmCCR1 fragment (523 bp) into the digested gel-purified IV-1.1.
Digest pGEM-T::ZmCCR1(285 bp) and IV-1.1::ZmCCR1(523 bp) with BglII and SacI.
Ligate the gel-purified 285 bp ZmCCR1 fragment into the digested 523 bp IV-1.1::ZmCCR1 fragment.
Clone both fragments into IV-1.1 to create a ZmCCR1 RNAi construct with an inverted repeat sequence and spacer.
Transfer the construct into Escherichia coli (E. coli) and grow them.
Perform a midi-prep size plasmid DNA isolation to obtain sufficient plasmid DNA for maize genetic transformation.
Place 60 mg of tungsten beads in a 1.5 ml tube.
Wash with 1 ml of 70% ethanol by vortexing for 2 min.
Incubate at 23°C for 10 min and centrifuge at 18,894 x g for 2 min, then discard the supernatant.
Wash with 1 ml of 100% ethanol three times, centrifuging each time for 2 min and discarding the supernatant.
Add 1 ml of sterile 50% glycerol to reach a concentration of 60 mg/ml of tungsten beads.
Place 50 μl (3 mg) of tungsten beads in a 1.5 ml tube with 5 μl (1 μg) of IV-1.1::ZmCCR1 RNAi plasmid DNA, 50 μl of 2.5 M CaCl2, and 20 μl of 0.1 M spermidine.
Vortex briefly after each addition to mix the reagents thoroughly.
Vortex the tungsten bead-DNA mixture briefly.
Centrifuge the mixture at 18,894 x g for 30 seconds.
Pour off the supernatant and resuspend the pellets in 140 μl of 70% ethanol.
Remove and discard the liquid.
Add 140 μl of 100% ethanol to the pellets.
Remove and discard the liquid.
Add 48 μl of 100% ethanol to the pellets.
Use immediately or store on ice for up to 4 hours prior to bombardment.
Place a 3-5 cm diameter Hi-II embryogenic maize calli in the middle of 100 mm Petri dishes containing N6OSM media at least 4 hours prior to bombardment.
Prepare the PSD-1000/He Particle Delivery device according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Sterilize the chamber wall with 70% ethanol.
Load a sterile 650 psi rupture disk into the sterile retaining cap.
Spread 5-6 μl of the M10-DNA solution onto the surface of a macrocarrier and dry briefly.
Load the macrocarrier and stopping screen into the microcarrier launch assembly.
Place the microcarrier launch assembly and maize calli in the chamber at a selected distance from the stopping screen (L2 = 6 cm).
Close the door of the device.
Accelerate in a vacuum of 27 psi against a wire mesh screen.
Press the fire button until the rupture disk bursts and helium pressure gauge drops to zero.
Incubate the bombarded calli in a Petri dish containing N6OSM for 16 hours in the dark at 27 °C.
Break the calli into about ten pieces and transfer them to N6E medium in Petri dishes.
Incubate the calli on N6E medium for 5 days in the dark at 27 °C.
Transfer the calli onto N6S medium (selection media) after 5 days.
Subculture all calli on selection medium every 30 days for 8-12 weeks without disturbing the calli structure.
Excise the white fast-growing tissues from the non-proliferating and partially necrotic mother calli after about 8-10 weeks.
Subculture the excised tissues to fresh selection medium (N6S).
Incubate as above for continued growth.
Transfer the white and fast growing embryonic calli onto regeneration medium.
Incubate on regeneration medium for 1 week.
Switch the regenerating embryogenic calli to a period of 16 hours daylight and 8 hours dark at 25-27 °C.
Transfer the regenerating shoots onto rooting medium in a glass test tube after 3-4 weeks.
Continue to incubate as above for another 5-6 days.
Wash the roots carefully under water tap once substantial root development appears.
Transplant the plantlets to 4” pots with soil.
Cover the pots with plastic bags to keep moist.
Make small holes in the plastic bags after 2 days.
Remove the plastic bags after 5-6 days.
Continue to incubate as above for another 5-6 days.
Transfer seedlings into 18” pots with soil and maintain in full summer sunlight or greenhouse light.
Fix maize leaf mid-ribs in 5 ml of 10% neutral buffered formalin.
Process and vacuum infiltrate with paraffin on a tissue processor using a tissue processor.
Embed tissues in paraffin using a HistoCentre III embedding station.
Remove excess paraffin from the edges once blocks are cooled.
Section sample at 4-5 μm with a microtome using a microtome.
Place sections on microscope slides and dry in a 56 °C incubator for 2-24 hr.
Deparaffinize sections in two changes of xylene for 5 min at 23 °C.
Hydrate slides through two changes of 100% ethanol for 2 min and two changes of 95% ethanol for 2 min at 23 °C.
Rinse the sections in running tap water for 2 min.
Stain with 0.05% toluidine blue O for 1-2 min and rinse briefly with ddH2O.
Place a coverslip on the samples with immersion oil and visualize with light microscopy.
Fix cross-sectioned maize leaf mid-ribs in 4% glutaraldehyde and 0.1 M sodium phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) at 4 °C for 1-2 hr.
Briefly rinse the samples in the buffer.
Dehydrate them in an ethanol series (25%, 50%, 75%, and 95%) for 10-15 min at each gradation and 100% ethanol for 10 min, 3x.
Dry the dehydrated cross-sectioned maize leaf mid-ribs in a critical point dryer using liquid carbon dioxide as the transitional fluid.
Mount the dried samples on aluminum stubs using high vacuum carbon tabs.
Coat the maize leaf mid-ribs mounted on aluminum stubs with gold (approximately 20 nm thickness) in a sputter coater purged with argon gas.
Examine the coated samples in a JEOL JSM-6400V scanning electron microscope.
Mill the samples through a 2 mm screen.
Determine the moisture content of each sample using a moisture analyzer and record the value.
Weigh out ~1.5 g of each sample and record the mass.

Extract the samples using water for the first extraction, followed by ethanol for the second extraction using either an automated solvent extractor (3 cycles per extraction, ~14 min per cycle) or soxhlet apparatus (8 hr per extraction).
Dry the extracted samples at 45 °C overnight, then allow them to cool in the desiccator, and weigh again.
Set an incubator to 30 °C.
Measure 0.3 g of each dry, extracted sample into screw-top high pressure tubes.
Record the weights to the nearest 0.1 mg.
Add 3 ml of 72% H2SO4 to each pressure tube.
Mix the sample using a glass or Teflon stir rod.
Leave the stir rod in the tube until water is added following incubation.
Place vials in an incubator set to 30 °C and 150 rpm for 60 min.
After 1 hr, add 84 ml of deionized water to dilute the acid concentration to 4%.
Mix with the stir rod carefully.
Tightly seal the stoppers on all vials.
Place sealed vials into a metal rack or large beakers.
Autoclave at 121 °C using a liquid sterilization cycle for 1 hr.
Allow them to cool to room temperature before opening.
Pre-ash the filtering crucibles in a furnace at 575 °C for at least 4 hr.
Allow crucibles to cool in a desiccator for at least an hour.
Vacuum filter the solution from each tube through a separate crucible, using a rubber adaptor to secure the crucible.
Use deionized water to rinse any remaining particles from the tube.
Dry the lignin residue at 105 °C for a minimum of 4 hr.
Record the weight of the dry crucible and residue.
Ramp from room temperature to 105 °C and hold for 12 min.
Ramp to 250 °C at 10 °C/min and hold for 30 min.
Ramp to 575 °C at 20 °C/min and hold for at least 180 min.
Remove the crucibles from the furnace and cool in a desiccator.
Weigh the crucible and ash.
Calculate the acid insoluble residue using the provided equation.
